::: {.callout-important}
## Status

**STUDY08-R2 — genomic inference successful but annotation inference remains
weak.** The one pre-specified replicate is complete. Evidence remains a local,
review-pending result; no reference capsule is claimed.
:::

## Why?

Studies 06 and 07 found difficult annotation-parameter inference in a
relatively low-information benchmark despite useful genomic inference. Study
08 asks whether that behavior improves in a deliberately high-information
positive control.

## What changed?

```text
N_train: 1400 -> 4500
M:       1500 -> 35000
```

The nonintercept annotation coefficients, total heritability, mixture effect
multipliers, and approximate absolute non-null architecture are preserved.
The larger panel therefore adds primarily null/background markers rather than
turning the design into a dramatically more polygenic phenotype.

Null markers are informative because annotation coefficients are learned from
differences in genomic-component probability across annotation values. They
therefore contribute marker-level null/non-null contrasts, although LD reduces
the effective number of independent observations.

## Methods

The only methods are SBayesR, ordinary joint SBayesRC, and ordinary joint
SBayesRC-S. All use the same training summary statistics, marker order,
sparse-LD CSR operator, and fixed-E residual contract. A qualification attempt
with residual updating failed at SBayesR iteration zero because the projected
CSR residual scale became negative; before any successful fit or method-output
inspection, all methods were therefore aligned to the already specified
`fixVe` contract. No EM or experimental sampler is included.

## Frozen design

The deterministic split contains 4,500 training and 500 validation samples.
The marker set is the first 35 complete, source-order, 1,000-marker blocks from
the 37,991 QC-qualified markers: 35,000 markers in total. The annotation matrix
has enriched-binary prevalence 0.15 and absolute pairwise correlations below
0.009. Sequential continuation-stick calibration gives intercepts -3.5264,
-0.3808, and -0.5213, with expected component counts 34,820 / 90 / 54 / 36.
The realized counts are 34,847 / 73 / 48 / 32 and realized heritability is
0.50.

## Results

Genomic inference was sensible for all methods. Beta correlations were 0.937
(SBayesR), 0.951 (SBayesRC), and 0.951 (SBayesRC-S); validation genetic-value
correlations were 0.931, 0.948, and 0.949. Thus annotation modeling did not
degrade genomic recovery.

The primary continuous-annotation result was negative. Joint SBayesRC had a
worst nonintercept alpha R-hat of 2.227 and minimum bulk ESS of 5.13. Its
nonintercept alpha RMSE was 0.369. Component priors were accurate in aggregate
(correlation 0.9997), but active-prior recovery was only 0.912 and was strongly
chain-sensitive: minimum chain-to-chain Pearson 0.514 and Spearman 0.190. This
is worse mixing than the frozen Study 07 stress case, not the hypothesized
positive-control improvement.

SBayesRC-S assigned pooled PIP 1.000 to `enriched_binary` and 0.997 to
`continuous_signal`, but 0.240 to `null_annotation`. The null PIP ranged from
0.016 to 0.742 across chains. Selection alpha mixing was also poor (worst
nonintercept R-hat 1.982; minimum bulk ESS 5.48), while `pi_A` had R-hat 1.071
and stick-specific `tau2` R-hats were 1.067, 1.032, and 1.005.

Wall-clock runtimes were 374 seconds for SBayesR, 677 seconds for SBayesRC, and
765 seconds for SBayesRC-S. Compact CSV tables and four figures are under the
ignored local Study 08 result directory for scientific review.

## Decision

The substantially larger N and M did not resolve ordinary joint annotation
mixing under this one-replicate design and final chain schedule. Because the
failure is large rather than borderline, this positive-control result is clear
enough to stop: no follow-up grid or additional replicate is proposed. This
does not isolate the causal contribution of N or M and does not establish a
general power relationship.

## Scope

This is one positive-control replicate. It cannot establish universal
annotation-PIP calibration or identify separate causal effects of sample size
and marker count, because both change together.
